title: Infrastructure simplification moves consistency logic into every caller
task: Review a proposal to remove a central invariant-enforcing component and let each caller implement the rule locally.
context: A shared component currently validates and normalizes identifiers before persistence.
The proposal removes it to make the core service smaller.
Each caller would then implement normalization and validation independently.
evidence: The normalization rule is identical across callers.
Past bugs occurred when one caller implemented the rule differently.
The shared component has a small stable API.
Removing it reduces one module but duplicates the invariant five times.
snippet: shared normalize_id(x) -> proposed per-caller normalization logic
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Remove the shared component because fewer modules means less complexity.
Treat caller duplication as harmless because each implementation is short.
Measure complexity only by code inside the core service.
expected_decision_properties: Identify the proposal as complexity displacement from one owned location to multiple callers.
Count multiplicity and divergence risk, not just local line count.
Avoid turning this into a universal rule that all shared helpers are good.
unacceptable_reasoning: Fewer modules always means simpler architecture.
Short duplicated logic is never a maintenance problem.
Centralization is automatically better regardless of ownership or bottleneck risk.
expected_tradeoffs: local simplicity vs repeated caller complexity
central invariant enforcement vs distributed flexibility
verification_expectations: Verify all callers use the same normalization contract.
Run regression tests for previously divergent inputs.
Confirm the shared boundary does not introduce a new performance or availability bottleneck.
